$comment: Mobile budgets of the main public templates (WEB-005), checked by web-vitals.spec.ts on the production build: 412 x 823 at 1.75x, 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbit/s down, 0.75 Mbit/s up, CPU slowed 4x, a returning visitor in English who chose Uzbekistan (the example hub's records, DEMO-US), median of three cold loads (browser cache disabled). Every page is rendered per request with the strict nonce Content Security Policy (architect's decision of 2026-10-31; full-page caching is deferred). Measured on 2026-10-31 (Apple M-series, local) with that strict policy: LCP 0.90-1.14 s, FCP 0.90-1.14 s, CLS 0, TBT 0.39-0.53 s; document 42.6-56.3 KiB, CSS 37.4-40.6 KiB, JS 374-383 KiB compressed. main before WEB-005, same profile: LCP 7.2-7.6 s, FCP 3.2-3.4 s, CSS 53 KiB on every template. On the CI browser job (a shared runner with three other test workers, every page rendered per request) the same version measured LCP and FCP 1.10-1.90 s and TBT 1.31-2.46 s (company template slowest). LCP and CLS budgets are the Web Vitals 'good' thresholds (2.5 s, 0.1); FCP is held to 2.5 s instead of the 'good' 1.8 s because per-request rendering on the shared runner measured 1.9 s for the company template; TBT is a regression guard at 3.5 s (the 'good' 200 ms is calibrated on Lighthouse's emulated device, not on a throttled shared runner). Byte budgets are about 15% above the measurement; scripts follow the CI-001 route budget. Raising a budget needs a reviewed reason.
